newsitem.title: MEXICO: SOCCER-HUGO SANCHEZ, MICHEL PLAY LAST GAMES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HUGO SANCHEZ, MICHEL PLAY LAST GAMES.

text.p: Former Spanish international Michel and Mexico's ex-international Hugo Sanchez both played the last game of their professional careers as they turned out for Atletico Celaya in the Mexican championship on Sunday.
The two players, team mates with Spanish giants Real Madrid during the late 1980s, were brought together again at Celaya last year.

Despite their presence, Celaya had a disappointing season and Sunday's 3-2 defeat away to reigning champions Santos Laguna meant they finished bottom of their group in the qualifying stage of their championship.
Sanchez, who was top scorer in the Spanish championship in four seasons with Real Madrid, scored only two goals in his stay at Celaya.
Michel, 34, joined the club after being relegated to the subtitutes' bench at Real Madrid, the only other club he played for.

Michel, full name Jose Miguel Gonzalez Martin, made his professional debut in 1984 and in 12 years with Real Madrid won the Spanish championship six times, the UEFA Cup twice and the Copa del Rey twice. He played for Spain in the 1986 and 1990 World Cups.
He announced his retirement during the week, saying: "This will be the last time I shall pull on a football shirt."

Sanchez, now 38, played for Rayo Vallencano in Spain, Dallas Burn in the United States, America and Atlante in Mexico and Linz in Austria after leaving Real Madrid, where he won the Spanish championship five times and the UEFA Cup once.
He ended his international career in the 1994 World Cup, where he was bitterly disappointed at playing only part of one match, against Norway. He also played in the 1986 World Cup.
Afterwards, Sanchez, who scored 44 goals in his 82 internationals, became a fierce critic of Miguel Mejia Baron, the Mexican coach at the time.
Sanchez also played for Real's great rivals Atletico Madrid and Mexican side UNAM earlier in his career.
Santos took a three-goal lead thanks to two goals by Jared Borguetti and one by Argentine striker Gabriel Caballero but Atletico pulled back two late goals through Hugo Santana and Salvador Reyes.
The win guaranteed Santos a place in the knock-out stage of the championship along with America, Guadalajara, Neza, UNAM, Atlante and Necaxa. Morelia and UAG play off for the other place.
